questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to constitutionalism in India, consider the following statements:
1. Constitutionalism holds that government power should be limited by constitutional rules.
2. Articles 13, 32 and 226 form the foundation of judicial review.
3. Article 50 directs the State to separate the judiciary from the executive in public services.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. The Supreme Court observed that majoritarianism cannot trump constitutionalism in a constitutional democracy.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to judicial pronouncements on constitutionalism, consider the following statements:
1. Kesavananda Bharati (1973) held that Parliament's amending power under Article 368 cannot alter the basic structure.
2. K.S. Puttaswamy (2017) held that the right to privacy is guaranteed under Article 21.
3. Navtej Singh Johar (2018) upheld the criminalisation of homosexuality.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Navtej Singh Johar decriminalised homosexuality. I.R. Coelho (2007) held constitutionalism requires control over exercise of governmental power.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to Public Interest Litigation (PIL), consider the following statements:
1. In PIL the petitioner must always be one of the two parties in the dispute.
2. Under PIL, a public-spirited person can file a petition on behalf of those who cannot approach the court themselves.
3. The term 'PIL' was first used in India by Justice V.K. Krishna Iyer and Justice P.N. Bhagwati.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: In PIL the petitioner may be a third party not personally involved in the dispute. Epistolary jurisdiction allows letters to be treated as writ petitions.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to landmark PIL cases, consider the following statements:
1. Hussainara Khatoon v. State of Bihar (1979) is regarded as the first recorded PIL, concerning under-trial prisoners.
2. Vishaka v. State of Rajasthan (1997) led to guidelines that later formed the basis of the POSH Act, 2013.
3. M.C. Mehta v. Union of India (1987) led to closure of industries discharging untreated effluents into the Ganga.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. In State of Uttarakhand v. Balwant Singh Chaufal (2010) the Court issued directions to preserve the purity of PILs and impose costs on busybodies.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to concerns about misuse of PIL, consider the following statements:
1. The Supreme Court is burdened with more than 3,500 PILs.
2. State of Jharkhand v. Shiv Shankar Sharma (2022) held that the bona fides of the petitioner are irrelevant.
3. 'Ambush PILs' are filed with the aim of securing dismissal and obstructing legitimate litigants.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The Court held that the bona fides of the PIL petitioner are an extremely relevant consideration that must be examined at the threshold.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the Panchayat Advancement Index (PAI) 2.0, consider the following statements:
1. It measures the progress of over 2.6 lakh Gram Panchayats and is anchored in the Localisation of SDGs.
2. The 17 SDGs are aggregated into 9 thematic areas.
3. Many Gram Panchayats fell in the highest Achiever category in PAI 2.0.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: No Gram Panchayat fell in the Achiever (A+) grade. About 1.4% were Front Runners, 45.72% Performers, 47.6% Aspirants and 5.27% Beginners. Tripura had 80% Front Runners.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the PAI categories and the Panchayati Raj framework, consider the following statements:
1. The Eleventh Schedule includes 18 subjects.
2. A Gram Panchayat scoring 90 and above is an Achiever (A+).
3. The 73rd Amendment, 1992 added Part IX (Articles 243-243O) and the Eleventh Schedule.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The Eleventh Schedule includes 29 subjects that States may transfer to Panchayats. PAI 2.0 recorded 97.30% participation with mandatory Gram Sabha validation.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the Election Commission of India under the Constitution, consider the following statements:
1. Article 324 vests superintendence, direction and control of elections in the Election Commission.
2. Other Election Commissioners enjoy the same constitutional protection against removal as the CEC.
3. The Chief Election Commissioner can be removed only like a Supreme Court judge.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Other Election Commissioners can be removed on the recommendation of the CEC. Article 329 bars court interference in electoral matters and elections can be challenged only through an election petition.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the appointment of Election Commissioners, consider the following statements:
1. In Anoop Baranwal (2023) the Supreme Court set up an interim Selection Committee of the PM, the Leader of Opposition and the CJI.
2. The 2023 Act replaced the CJI with a Union Cabinet Minister on the Selection Committee.
3. A Search Committee headed by the Chief Justice proposes a shortlist of five names.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: A Search Committee headed by the Cabinet Secretary proposes five names, and the Selection Committee may bypass the shortlist. The 2023 Act repealed the 1991 Act, and the SC called the mechanism 'Tyranny of the Elected'.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to proposals on the selection of Election Commissioners, consider the following statements:
1. In the United States, appointments to the Election Commission need no legislative confirmation.
2. The Tarkunde Committee, Goswami Committee and the Law Commission (255th Report) recommended a collegium of the PM, the Leader of Opposition and the CJI.
3. The 2nd ARC recommended a collegium including the PM, the Speaker, the LoP, the Law Minister and the Deputy Chairman of Rajya Sabha.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: In the US the President appoints the members but the selection requires confirmation by the Senate. In Canada appointments are made by a resolution of the House of Commons.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the National Sports Governance Act, 2025 and its rules, consider the following statements:
1. Sports is Entry 33 of the State List in the Seventh Schedule.
2. The CAG cannot audit the accounts of the Board.
3. The National Sports Board has a Chairperson and two Members appointed by the Centre on the recommendation of a Search-cum-Selection Committee.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The CAG is empowered to audit the accounts of the Board. Members serve 3 years or until 65 years, whichever is earlier, with one reappointment allowed.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the National Sports Tribunal Rules, 2026, consider the following statements:
1. The Chairperson serves for 5 years or till 70 years of age.
2. The Members serve for 5 years or till 67 years.
3. Tribunal orders are not enforceable like decrees of a civil court.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Tribunal orders are enforceable like civil court decrees and become final after the appeal period. The National Sports Policy 2025 replaced the 2001 policy.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the NITI Aayog report on Million-Plus Cities, consider the following statements:
1. The report recommends that mayors be indirectly elected for a flexible tenure.
2. India's 47 million-plus cities account for nearly one-third of the urban population and 60% of GDP.
3. City governments have full control, on average, over only 4 of the 18 functions listed under the 74th Amendment.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: It recommends directly elected Mayors with fixed tenure and an empowered Mayor-in-Council. It also recommends integrating water, sanitation and transport under city governments.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the Citizenship (Amendment) Rules, 2026, consider the following statements:
1. Applicants under the CAA, 2019 must declare whether they hold a valid or expired passport from Pakistan, Afghanistan or Bangladesh.
2. OCI applications can still be made offline at consulates only.
3. A minor child cannot hold the passport of another country while holding an Indian passport.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: OCI processes including registration are now completely online through a portal and e-OCI can be issued in electronic format. Revisions against OCI orders go to an authority one rank higher.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) scheme, consider the following statements:
1. It was introduced through the Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2005 and the PIO scheme was merged with it in 2015.
2. OCI gives a multiple-entry, multi-purpose lifelong visa to visit India.
3. OCI confers the right to vote and hold constitutional posts.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: OCI does not confer political rights such as voting or holding constitutional posts. It is a privilege and not an entitlement, and offers parity with NRIs except in acquiring agricultural or plantation property.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the Tenth Schedule of the Constitution, consider the following statements:
1. The decision on disqualification is made by the High Court.
2. It was added by the Fifty-Second Amendment Act, 1985.
3. A member is not disqualified if the original party merges with another and at least two-thirds of members agree.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The Speaker or Chairman adjudicates disqualification. The 91st Amendment removed the one-third split provision, and a nominated member joining a party after six months is disqualified.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the Prison Statistics India 2024 report of the NCRB, consider the following statements:
1. The prison occupancy rate fell from 120.8% in 2023 to 112.7% in 2024.
2. About 95.8% of prisoners were male.
3. There are 34 women's jails, and 21 States and UTs have none.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. The e-Prisons project is by the NIC, and the Supreme Court's FASTER system speeds communication of bail orders.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Bill, 2026, consider the following statements:
1. It seeks to raise the Supreme Court strength from 33 to 37, excluding the CJI.
2. Article 124 empowers Parliament to determine the number of judges.
3. The 1956 Act originally fixed the number of judges at 10 excluding the CJI.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. The strength was raised by amendments in 1960, 1977, 1986, 2008 and 2019, and the Supreme Court has about 92,926 pending cases.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the e-Courts Mission Mode Project, consider the following statements:
1. It was launched in 2007 under the National e-Governance Plan.
2. It is implemented by the Department of Justice under the guidance of the Supreme Court's e-Committee.
3. Sikkim was declared the first paperless State judiciary.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. A paperless judiciary uses digital files, e-filing, online hearings and digital case tracking.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the National Compliance Reduction and Deregulation initiative, consider the following statements:
1. A Task Force was constituted in 2025 under the Cabinet Secretary.
2. It identified 23 priority areas across 5 broad sectors.
3. Tripura was the first State to complete all priority areas under Deregulation Phase-II.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. Phase II was rolled out in January 2026 and covers land, utilities, environment, education, health and labour.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to India-US relations, consider the following statements:
1. India is designated a Major Defense Partner of the US.
2. India has signed LEMOA, COMCASA and BECA with the US.
3. The US imposed a 50% tariff on certain Indian exports in 2025, which was later reduced after an interim trade agreement.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. The TRUST initiative covers AI, semiconductors, quantum and telecom, and the NISAR mission is a NASA-ISRO collaboration.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to the irritants in India-US relations, consider the following statements:
1. India's purchase of discounted Russian crude is a flashpoint.
2. India has given up multi-alignment and joined the US camp.
3. The US raised concerns on India's purchase of the S-400 under CAATSA.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: India insists on multi-alignment, engaging with the Quad as well as BRICS and the SCO. H-1B visa restrictions also affect Indian professionals.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to the visit of the Prime Minister to Norway and Sweden and the 3rd India-Nordic Summit, consider the following statements:
1. India-Norway ties were elevated to a Green Strategic Partnership.
2. India and Sweden upgraded relations to a Strategic Partnership.
3. Norway announced participation in India's Indo-Pacific Oceans Initiative.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. IPOI was launched by India at the East Asia Summit in 2019 and builds on SAGAR.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to the Nordic region, consider the following statements:
1. The Nordic region comprises Denmark, Finland, Iceland, Norway and Sweden.
2. Scandinavia strictly includes only Denmark, Norway and Sweden.
3. All five Nordic nations are members of the Arctic Council.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. The Faroe Islands, Greenland and Aland are autonomous territories, and the Nordic Council was established in 1952.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to India and the Arctic, consider the following statements:
1. India's research station 'Himadri' was established in July 2008 at Ny-Alesund, Norway.
2. India has been an observer in the Arctic Council since 2013.
3. ISRO uses Norway's Svalbard ground station for satellite data reception.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. India's Arctic policy has six pillars, and EFTA includes Norway and Iceland, with whom India signed the TEPA.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to the India-UAE Strategic Defence Partnership framework visit, consider the following statements:
1. An MoU scales the UAE's participation in India's Strategic Petroleum Reserves to 30 million barrels.
2. India and the UAE agreed to explore Indian strategic crude storage at Fujairah.
3. CDAC and G42 agreed to set up an 8 Exaflop super computing cluster.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. The UAE is the only foreign nation participating in India's SPR programme, and a Virtual Trade Corridor using MAITRI was operationalised.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q:
With reference to the United Arab Emirates, consider the following statements:
1. It is a federation of seven emirates.
2. Fujairah is the only emirate with no frontage along the Persian Gulf.
3. The Tropic of Cancer passes through the Abu Dhabi emirate.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. The federation includes Abu Dhabi, Dubai, Sharjah, Ajman, Umm al-Quwain, Ras al-Khaimah and Fujairah.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to the importance of the UAE for India, consider the following statements:
1. India and the UAE negotiated the CEPA in 2022 in a record 90 days.
2. Bilateral merchandise trade reached USD 101.25 billion in FY 2025-26.
3. UPI is linked with the UAE's AANI and RuPay with JAYWAN.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. The UAE hosts 3.5 to 4 million Indians and is the third-largest trading partner. India's trade deficit with it was USD 26.8 billion in 2024-25.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to the India-Italy Special Strategic Partnership, consider the following statements:
1. The target is to expand bilateral trade to 20 billion euros by 2029.
2. 2027 will be celebrated as the Year of Culture and Tourism between India and Italy.
3. Italy signed an MoU to participate in the National Maritime Heritage Complex at Lothal.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. The Prime Minister received the Agricola Award at FAO in Rome, and Italy exited the BRI in 2023 after joining it in 2019.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to the issues in India-Italy relations, consider the following statements:
1. Indian labourers face exploitation in Italy's agricultural sector under the caporalato system.
2. Italy has historically supplied weapons to Pakistan.
3. Leonardo is Italy's largest defence firm and faced restrictions after the VVIP helicopter scandal.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. Italy hosts the largest Indian diaspora in the European Union, and IMEC was announced in 2023.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to the 11th Review Conference of the NPT, consider the following statements:
1. It concluded without a consensus outcome document as the US and Iran sparred.
2. This was the third consecutive review without agreement.
3. India is a party to the NPT.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: India is not a party and considers the NPT a biased framework dividing the world into nuclear haves and have-nots. The NPT entered into force in 1970.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to global nuclear governance, consider the following statements:
1. The Outer Space Treaty permits placing nuclear weapons in Earth's orbit.
2. The IAEA was set up in 1957.
3. India ratified the IAEA Additional Protocol in 2014.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The Outer Space Treaty, 1967 prohibits placing nuclear weapons in orbit or on celestial bodies. The Seabed Treaty of 1971 bans nuclear weapons on the ocean floor beyond a 12-mile zone.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to nuclear governance treaties and regimes, consider the following statements:
1. The CTBT bans all nuclear test explosions, and India has not signed it.
2. The Nuclear Suppliers Group was established after India's 1974 nuclear test, and India is a member.
3. The Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons came into force in 2021.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: India is not a member of the NSG though it seeks membership. India joined the MTCR in 2016, the Wassenaar Arrangement in 2017 and the Australia Group in 2018.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to nuclear-weapon-free zones, consider the following statements:
1. The Treaty of Tlatelolco covers Latin America.
2. The Treaty of Pelindaba covers Africa.
3. The Treaty of Rarotonga covers Southeast Asia.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Rarotonga covers the South Pacific and Bangkok covers Southeast Asia. Only 9 countries possess nuclear weapons, and about 12,241 warheads existed in early 2024.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to the exit of the UAE from OPEC and OPEC+, consider the following statements:
1. India is a member of OPEC.
2. OPEC was created at the Baghdad Conference in 1960 and is headquartered in Vienna.
3. After the UAE's exit, OPEC has 11 members.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: India is not a member. OPEC+ was formed in 2016 by OPEC and 10 other producers and has historically controlled about 41% of global oil supply.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to crude oil benchmarks, consider the following statements:
1. Brent crude is based on light sweet crude streams from the North Sea.
2. Dubai/Oman is a light, sweet crude benchmark used for American exports.
3. West Texas Intermediate is priced at Cushing, Oklahoma.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Dubai/Oman is a medium, sour crude benchmark used to price Middle Eastern exports to Asian markets.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to the India-New Zealand Free Trade Agreement, consider the following statements:
1. New Zealand will eliminate duties on all Indian exports.
2. New Zealand committed to USD 20 billion investment in India over 15 years.
3. India offered market access in all tariff lines with no exclusions.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: India offered access in about 70% of tariff lines, with about 30% excluded to shield sectors like dairy, sugar and onions. An annual quota of 5,000 temporary employment visas was agreed.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to India-Vietnam relations, consider the following statements:
1. Relations were upgraded to an Enhanced Comprehensive Strategic Partnership.
2. The bilateral trade target is USD 25 billion by 2030.
3. Vietnam joined the Indo-Pacific Oceans Initiative.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. 13 MoUs were signed, including one on digitisation of ancient Cham manuscripts.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to the India-EU Trade and Technology Council, consider the following statements:
1. The recent battery recycling initiative is funded only by India's Ministry of Heavy Industries.
2. It was launched in February 2023.
3. It has three core working groups.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The EUR 15.2 million initiative is funded by the EU's Horizon Europe programme and India's Ministry of Heavy Industries.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to the Thucydides Trap, consider the following statements:
1. The term was coined by Graham Allison.
2. It refers to the danger of conflict when a rising power threatens to displace a dominant power.
3. The Peloponnesian War between Athens and Sparta started in 431 BC.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. It is used to analyse US-China relations.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to freedom of navigation under UNCLOS, consider the following statements:
1. The territorial sea extends up to 12 nautical miles.
2. Innocent passage applies only to merchant ships and not to warships.
3. The Exclusive Economic Zone extends up to 200 nautical miles.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Innocent passage applies to merchant ships and even warships. The Strait of Hormuz is governed by transit passage under UNCLOS.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to the Persian Gulf Strait Authority and AIIB, consider the following statements:
1. Iran announced a regulatory body, the PGSA, to oversee operations in the Strait of Hormuz.
2. Vessels would need transit permits from it before entering the Strait.
3. The AIIB launched a USD 10 billion facility for members affected by the Middle East conflict.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. The facility is over two years for energy, food security and economic resilience.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to the SIPRI factsheet on multilateral peace operations, consider the following statements:
1. There were 58 active peacekeeping operations in 34 countries in 2025.
2. All top 10 military and police contributors, including India, are from the Global South.
3. A UN funding shortfall of about USD 2 billion forced cuts in personnel.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. The EU redirected its European Peace Facility funds from Africa towards Ukraine and West Asia.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to the Global Report on Food Crises 2026, consider the following statements:
1. More than 266 million people in 47 countries faced acute food insecurity in 2025.
2. Conflict has overtaken extreme weather as the main driver.
3. The Global Network Against Food Crises was launched by the IMF in 2016.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: It was launched in 2016 by FAO with the EU and WFP at the World Humanitarian Summit. The WFP was established in 1961 and is headquartered in Rome.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to global migration, consider the following statements:
1. The Global Compact for Safe, Orderly and Regular Migration was adopted in December 2018 and is non-legally binding.
2. The International Migration Review Forum is held every four years.
3. The World Migration Report 2026 says about 304 million people lived outside their country of birth in 2024.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. India-UAE and India-US are the fifth and sixth largest migration corridors.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q:
With reference to places in the news, consider the following statements:
1. The Falkland Islands are an overseas territory of the UK in the South Atlantic claimed by Argentina.
2. Pratas (Dongsha) Island is a coral atoll in the South China Sea governed by Taiwan.
3. Belgorod is a region in south-western Russia bordering Ukraine.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. A war was fought over the Falklands in 1982.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to the B'nei Menashe community, consider the following statements:
1. They are a tribe from Arunachal Pradesh.
2. They are a Jewish-identifying community from Manipur and Mizoram.
3. They claim descent from the Tribe of Menashe, one of the Ten Lost Tribes of Israel.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: They belong to the Mizo-Kuki tribes of Manipur and Mizoram. Over 240 members were relocated to Tel Aviv.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the NITI Aayog roadmap 'DPI@2047 for Viksit Bharat', consider the following statements:
1. It recommends DPI 2.0 for 2025-2035 to drive livelihood-led growth.
2. Its first cycle in 2026-27 focuses on health and education.
3. DPI 2.0 has eight sectoral transformations including MSMEs, agriculture, education and health.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The first cycle focuses on MSME and agriculture transformations with lighthouse pilots in six States. A neutral ecosystem body for global engagement is to be set up by 2027.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the impact of Digital Public Infrastructure in India, consider the following statements:
1. DPI contributed 0.9% to GDP in 2022, with a projection of 4.2% by 2030.
2. India reached 80% bank account penetration in eight years, which BIS estimated would have taken 47 years.
3. DBT has saved Rs 3.48 lakh crore through leakage prevention.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. India had signed DPI MoUs with 24 countries as of February 2026, and the New Delhi Leaders' Declaration at the G20 recognised DPI as a development accelerator.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to components of India's DPI stack, consider the following statements:
1. ABHA is the Ayushman Bharat Health Account.
2. AgriStack is a farmer-centric DPI for interoperable land, crop and scheme data.
3. DigiYatra is a facial recognition-based system for air travel.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. Other components include the Account Aggregator framework, ONDC, DigiLocker, UMANG, DIKSHA and PM GatiShakti.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the Unified Payments Interface and its variants, consider the following statements:
1. UPI completed 10 years, with transactions rising from 2 crore in 2016-17 to 24,162 crore in 2025-26.
2. UPI LITE is an on-device wallet for low-value transactions below Rs 1,000.
3. UPI One World is a wallet for Indians living abroad only.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: UPI One World is a PPI wallet powered by UPI for foreign nationals arriving in India and NRIs. UPI LITE X allows offline payments, and UPI Cash Point allows cash withdrawal at shops.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to global recognition of UPI, consider the following statements:
1. The IMF in June 2025 recognised UPI as the world's largest retail fast payment system by volume.
2. UPI accounts for about 49% of global real-time payment transaction volume as per a 2024 ACI Worldwide report.
3. UPI is live in over 8 countries.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. Challenges include the zero-MDR sustainability dilemma and market concentration in a few third-party apps.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the new series of the Index of Industrial Production, consider the following statements:
1. The base year has been revised from 2011-12 to 2022-23.
2. The item basket has been expanded from 839 to 1,042 products.
3. Gas supply, water supply and sewerage and waste management have been added to the coverage.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. The electricity index now separately tracks renewable and non-renewable generation.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the methodology of the IIP, consider the following statements:
1. The IIP is compiled using the Paasche index formula.
2. A chain-linked IIP is being introduced alongside the fixed-base index.
3. The geometric mean method is used to link the 2011-12 and 2022-23 series.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The IIP uses the Laspeyres fixed-base volume index. It is released monthly by the NSO with a lag of 28 days, and the first IIP was released with 1937 as base year.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the IFAD Country Strategic Opportunities Programme (COSOP) 2026-2033, consider the following statements:
1. It was launched by the Government of India with the International Fund for Agricultural Development.
2. It places emphasis on SHGs, FPOs and rural cooperatives as platforms to link people with finance and markets.
3. A parallel agreement was signed with NABARD.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. Challenges include a workforce share of about 46% in agriculture against about 18% of GDP, and over 85% small and marginal farmers.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to Farmer Producer Organisations (FPOs) in India, consider the following statements:
1. They can be registered under Part IXA of the Companies Act or under a Co-operative Societies Act.
2. The Small Farmers' Agribusiness Consortium (SFAC) supports State Governments in forming FPOs.
3. Farmers are first mobilised into Farmer Interest Groups of 15-20 members at village level.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. Under the scheme for 10,000 FPOs, up to Rs 18 lakh management cost support is given for 3 years, and CBBOs link FPOs to markets.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the capital adequacy framework for banks in India, consider the following statements:
1. CRAR is computed as (Tier 1 + Tier 2 capital) divided by risk-weighted assets.
2. Additional Tier 1 capital forms part of Common Equity Tier 1.
3. The RBI minimum CET1 ratio of 5.5% and CRAR of 9% are stricter than the Basel III baseline of 4.5% and 8%.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: CET1 comprises common shares, retained earnings and reserves; AT1 is a separate component of Tier 1. The RBI now allows quarterly profits to be counted in CET1 for computing CRAR.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the Startup India Fund of Funds 2.0, consider the following statements:
1. It has a corpus of Rs 10,000 crore across the 16th and 17th Finance Commission cycles.
2. SIDBI is the initial Implementing Agency.
3. It invests directly in startups through equity.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The scheme invests only through SEBI-registered Category I and II Alternative Investment Funds; government share in any selected AIF cannot exceed 50% of its corpus.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the proposed Index of Service Production (ISP), consider the following statements:
1. It is intended to capture the informal services sector exclusively.
2. It is proposed to have 2024-25 as the base year.
3. It would draw on GST data and administrative data from sectoral ministries.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The ISP is designed to track the formal sector (trade, transport, banking, insurance, real estate, communication). MoSPI released the approach paper.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to LEADS and the logistics sector in India, consider the following statements:
1. LEADS is released by the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade.
2. LEADS 2025 uses a four-tier performance framework.
3. Logistics cost in India is about 8% of GDP.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. Over 60% of freight moves by road, and the National Logistics Policy was launched in 2022.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the recent changes in India's FDI rules, consider the following statements:
1. Foreign entities with up to 10% Chinese shareholding may invest in India under the automatic route.
2. Foreign investment in LIC is now allowed up to 49%.
3. 100% FDI is allowed in private insurance companies under the automatic route.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Foreign investment in LIC remains capped at 20%. The changes were notified through the Foreign Exchange Management (Second Amendment) Rules, 2026, and the 2020 curbs on land-border countries had been imposed through Press Note 3.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the Bharat Maritime Insurance Pool, consider the following statements:
1. GIC Re acts as the Pool Administrator.
2. It covers hull and machinery, cargo, P&I and war risks.
3. Claims above 100 million dollars trigger a sovereign guarantee.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. The pool has capacity of 1.5 billion dollars and sovereign guarantee of Rs 12,980 crore; it is administered by the Department of Financial Services.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the BHAVYA Scheme, consider the following statements:
1. It is a Central Sector Scheme that targets 100 plug-and-play industrial parks.
2. Funding is provided mainly as equity through the National Industrial Corridor Development and Investment Trust.
3. It runs for 6 years from 2026-27 with an outlay of Rs 33,660 crore.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. Minimum land is 100 acres for non-hilly states and 25 acres for hilly states, NE states and UTs.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the Emergency Credit Line Guarantee Scheme (ECLGS) 5.0, consider the following statements:
1. It provides 100% guarantee coverage for MSMEs and 90% for non-MSMEs and airlines.
2. Loans to the airline sector have a tenor of 7 years including a 2-year moratorium.
3. Guarantees are managed by NABARD.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Guarantees are provided by the National Credit Guarantee Trustee Company Ltd (NCGTC). The scheme falls under the Department of Financial Services.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to Electronic Gold Receipts (EGRs), consider the following statements:
1. The National Stock Exchange was the first to launch EGRs in India.
2. They are regulated by SEBI as securities under the SCRA, 1956.
3. They can be redeemed for physical gold, unlike gold ETFs which are cash settled.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The Bombay Stock Exchange was first to launch EGRs, in 2022. The gold is stored in SEBI-accredited vaults.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the TEAM (Trade Enablement and Access to Market) Initiative, consider the following statements:
1. It is a Central Sector Scheme launched in 2024.
2. It is a sub-scheme under the World Bank-supported RAMP Programme.
3. It helps micro and small enterprises sell through the Open Network for Digital Commerce.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. NSIC is the implementing agency and the duration is 2024 to 2027.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
RBI approved a record surplus transfer of Rs 2.86 lakh crore for 2025-26. Which of the following are sources of RBI income?
1. Interest on rupee securities
2. Liquidity adjustment facility
3. Marginal standing facility
4. Printing of notes
How many of the above are sources of income?
questions.why: Printing of notes is an expenditure item, along with agency charges and employee cost. RBI is not liable to income tax.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: Which authority regulates Electronic Gold Receipts in India?
questions.why: EGRs are securities under the SCRA 1956 and are regulated by SEBI.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The Mizoram Ginger Mission relates to which of the following?
opts: Promoting the cultivation of Mizo bird-eye chilli
Promoting organic turmeric farming in the State
questions.why: It was launched by MDoNER with the Government of Mizoram. Ginger needs warm humid climate and well-drained loamy soil.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the Indian Navy Maritime Security Strategy 2026, consider the following statements:
1. It is the third public articulation of India's naval strategy, after Freedom to Use the Seas (2007) and Ensuring Secure Seas (2015).
2. It describes India as a 'Net Security Provider' for the first time.
3. It addresses the 'No War No Peace' paradigm and grey-zone actions.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The 'Net Security Provider' role was already defined in Ensuring Secure Seas (2015), which also widened the focus from the east coast of Africa to the Western Pacific.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to India's maritime security environment, consider the following statements:
1. India has a coastline of 11,098.81 km and 1,389 islands.
2. About 95% of trade by volume and 68% by value moves by sea.
3. Undersea cables carry over 95% of intercontinental internet and voice traffic.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. Sea routes carry 88% of India's crude oil imports, and India has 12 major ports and 217 non-major ports.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to maritime threats, consider the following statements:
1. Dark vessels and shadow fleets disable AIS to evade sanctions and detection.
2. IUU fishing stands for Illegal, Unreported and Unregulated fishing.
3. Hybrid threats include maritime militias and deniable operations.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct and are listed among threats in INMSS-2026.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the Directorate of Enforcement, consider the following statements:
1. It functions under the Department of Revenue in the Ministry of Finance.
2. It was established in 1956 as an Enforcement Unit to enforce FERA, 1947.
3. It is responsible for enforcing the Fugitive Economic Offenders Act, 2018.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. ED also implements FEMA 1999 and PMLA 2002; the FY 2025-26 report shows 657 prosecution complaints and about 94% conviction rate.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to money laundering and its regulation in India, consider the following statements:
1. The UN Vienna Convention of 1988 contains provisions against money laundering linked to drug trafficking.
2. The Financial Intelligence Unit-India has brought Virtual Digital Asset Service Providers under anti-money laundering obligations.
3. India is not a member of the Financial Action Task Force.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: India is a member of FATF. The Palermo Convention of 2000 (UNTOC) also criminalises money laundering.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the Chief of Defence Staff (CDS), consider the following statements:
1. The post was created in 2019 on the lines of the Group of Ministers recommendation of 2001.
2. The CDS is the ex-officio Secretary of the Department of Military Affairs.
3. The CDS is the Chairman of the Chiefs of Staff Committee permanently.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. The CDS is the Principal Military Adviser to the Raksha Mantri on tri-service matters and the military adviser to the Nuclear Command Authority; the idea traces to the K. Subrahmanyam Committee.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to defence developments, consider the following statements:
1. India is the third largest military spender in the world as per SIPRI 2025.
2. The Advanced Medium Combat Aircraft is a 5th-generation stealth multirole fighter developed by the Aeronautical Development Agency.
3. AMCA Mk1 is planned with GE-F414 engines, and Mk2 with indigenous engines.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: India is the fifth biggest spender with 92.1 billion dollars (3.2% of global spending, up 8.9%). The five biggest are the US, China, Russia, Germany and India.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to recent Indian weapon systems, consider the following statements:
1. Divyastra is an Agni missile with MIRV capability.
2. Vayu Astra-1 is a loitering munition tested to 100 km range with a 10 kg warhead.
3. TARA converts unguided bombs into precision-guided glide weapons.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. TARA was developed by Research Centre Imarat, Hyderabad, with glide speed above 650 km/h and range over 80 km.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to Project 17A of the Indian Navy, consider the following statements:
1. Project 17A ships are the Nilgiri-class stealth frigates.
2. They are designed by the Warship Design Bureau.
3. They use a Combined Diesel or Gas propulsion plant.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. Mahendragiri was the sixth ship and the fourth built by Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders; others are Nilgiri, Himgiri, Udaygiri, Taragiri and Dunagiri.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to border management in India, consider the following statements:
1. India shares a land border of about 15,106.7 km with seven countries.
2. BOLD-QIT is a smart fencing project of the Assam Rifles on the India-Myanmar border.
3. CIBMS integrates sensors, radars, cameras and command-and-control systems along the border.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: BOLD-QIT (Border Electronically Dominated QRT Interception Technique) was launched by the Border Security Force along the India-Bangladesh border.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to TATP and Captagon, consider the following statements:
1. TATP is an organic peroxide explosive that is extremely sensitive to impact and heat.
2. Captagon mainly contains fenetylline and amphetamine.
3. Operation RAGEPILL was an NCB operation against a Captagon syndicate.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. Fenetylline and amphetamine are psychotropic substances under the NDPS Act 1985, and Captagon is placed under Schedule II of the 1971 UN Convention on Psychotropic Substances.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q: Exercise PRAGATI 2026 held at Umroi Military Station is led by which of the following?
questions.why: It has 12 Indian Ocean region participants; PRAGATI expands to Partnership of Regional Armies for Growth and Transformation in the Indian Ocean Region.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q: The Naval Anti-ship Missile-Short Range (NASM-SR) has been developed by:
questions.why: It uses a solid booster, a long-burn sustainer, an imaging infra-red seeker and a fibre optic gyroscope INS.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
With reference to the circular economy in India, consider the following statements:
1. It departs from the linear take-make-dispose model by promoting reuse, repair, refurbishing and recycling.
2. The Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026 mandate four-stream segregation at source.
3. India's e-waste recycling rate is higher than the global average.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: India's e-waste recycling rate is about 10% against the global average of about 22%. India is the world's third-largest e-waste generator.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
With reference to policy initiatives for waste and recycling in India, consider the following statements:
1. The Battery Waste Management Rules, 2022 prohibit landfill disposal and incineration of waste batteries.
2. The National Critical Mineral Mission, 2025 aims at developing domestic recycling capacity for critical minerals.
3. A Circular Economy Cell has been constituted in NITI Aayog.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. A unified EPR portal is being developed by MoEFCC, and the EPR framework is shifting from collection-based to recycling-based.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
With reference to Small Hydro Power in India, consider the following statements:
1. Himachal Pradesh has the highest small hydro potential among all Indian regions combined.
2. Hydropower projects of up to 25 MW capacity are classified as small hydro and administered by the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy.
3. The Northern Region has the highest small hydro potential.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Himachal Pradesh leads within the Northern Region (3,460 MW) which has about 7,978 MW or 38% of total potential. India has an estimated 21,133.61 MW potential, of which about 24.5% has been harnessed.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
With reference to the Small Hydro Power Development Scheme, consider the following statements:
1. It runs for five years from 2026-27 to 2030-31 with an outlay of Rs 2,584.60 crore.
2. It aims to add about 1,500 MW of new capacity.
3. For projects in the North-Eastern States, financial assistance is Rs 3.6 crore per MW or 30% of project cost, whichever is lower.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. The ceiling is Rs 30 crore per project in the North-East and Rs 20 crore elsewhere; DPR support is planned for at least 200 projects.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
With reference to coal gasification in India, consider the following statements:
1. Coal gasification converts coal into syngas, a mixture mainly of carbon monoxide and hydrogen.
2. The scheme mandates a single imported gasification technology.
3. The Union Cabinet approved an incentive scheme of Rs 37,500 crore for surface coal and lignite gasification.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The scheme is technology-agnostic while encouraging indigenous technology. Indian coal has 30-45% ash, so fluidised-bed gasifiers are favoured. Incentive is capped at Rs 5,000 crore per project.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
With reference to the Scheme for Promotion of Surface Coal/Lignite Gasification, consider the following statements:
1. It builds on the National Coal Gasification Mission launched in 2021.
2. Beneficiaries are selected through competitive bidding.
3. It is expected to create about 50,000 direct and indirect jobs across 25 projects.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. The scheme is under the Ministry of Coal and aims at substituting imports of methanol, ammonia and LNG.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
With reference to Marine Carbon Dioxide Removal (mCDR), consider the following statements:
1. Restoring mangroves and seagrass and ocean alkalinity enhancement are examples of mCDR.
2. The oceans store over 50 times more carbon than the atmosphere.
3. mCDR can replace deep emission reductions.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: mCDR can complement but not replace deep emission reductions. Challenges include monitoring, reporting and verification, standards and governance gaps.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
With reference to the International Big Cat Alliance, consider the following statements:
1. Its headquarters are in Nairobi.
2. It was launched in 2023 on the 50th anniversary of Project Tiger.
3. It aims at conserving seven big cats including the lion, tiger, snow leopard, leopard, cheetah, jaguar and puma.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Its headquarters are in India. Saudi Arabia became the 26th member, and India gave initial support of Rs 150 crore for five years.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q:
With reference to dams in India, consider the following statements:
1. India has the third largest number of large dams after the United States and China.
2. Gujarat has the highest number of specified dams.
3. About 98.5% of specified dams are owned by State Governments.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Maharashtra has the highest number of specified dams, followed by Madhya Pradesh and Gujarat. Around 26% of dams are over 50 years old.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q:
With reference to dam safety in India, consider the following statements:
1. The Dam Safety Act, 2021 creates a National Committee on Dam Safety and a National Dam Safety Authority.
2. DRIP Phase I introduced the DHARMA application for monitoring dam health.
3. DRIP Phases II and III are financed by the World Bank and the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. Phases II and III cover 736 dams across 19 states and three central agencies; eAabhas is an AI/ML and IoT-based platform for flood forecasting.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q:
With reference to El Niño and its impact on India, consider the following statements:
1. ENSO has three phases: El Niño, La Niña and neutral.
2. El Niño typically weakens the south-west monsoon.
3. A negative Indian Ocean Dipole reduces the negative impact of El Niño on the monsoon.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: A positive IOD, with the western Indian Ocean warmer, can offset El Niño's effect; a negative IOD can worsen drought. The droughts of 2002 and 2009 were linked to El Niño.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q:
With reference to El Niño Modoki and the term 'Super El Niño', consider the following statements:
1. El Niño Modoki involves warming mainly in the central Pacific.
2. 'Super El Niño' is an informal term and not an official WMO category.
3. El Niño got its name from Peruvian fishermen who observed warm waters around Christmas.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. The WMO ranked 2025 among the three warmest years recorded.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
With reference to the AI-enabled monsoon advance forecast launched by the Ministry of Earth Sciences, consider the following statements:
1. It was developed solely by ISRO.
2. It is the first AI-driven monsoon advance forecasting system developed by IMD and partners.
3. It provides probabilistic forecasts every Wednesday up to four weeks ahead.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: It was developed jointly by IMD, IITM Pune and NCMRWF. It supports farmers in 16 States and over 3,000 sub-districts.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the seven big cats covered by the International Big Cat Alliance?
questions.why: The seven are lion, tiger, snow leopard, leopard, cheetah, jaguar and puma.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: Under the Dam Safety Act, 2021, which is the apex body?
questions.why: NDSA is the regulatory and implementing arm, with state-level committees and organisations below.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
With reference to the SEHAT initiative, consider the following statements:
1. It is a joint initiative of ICMR and ICAR.
2. It includes development of biofortified and nutrient-dense crop varieties.
3. It includes One Health preparedness at the human-animal-environment interface.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. SEHAT stands for Science Excellence for Health through Agricultural Transformation and has five priority areas.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
With reference to the Petersberg Climate Dialogue and the Conference on Transitioning Away from Fossil Fuels, consider the following statements:
1. The Petersberg Climate Dialogue is an informal annual ministerial meeting initiated by Germany in 2010.
2. The Conference replaces the UNFCCC negotiating process.
3. The first Conference on Transitioning Away from Fossil Fuels was hosted by Colombia and the Netherlands.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The Conference is not a negotiating body and does not replace the UNFCCC. It was announced at COP30 and launched the Science Panel for the Global Energy Transition.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
With reference to the Methane Alert and Response System (MARS), consider the following statements:
1. It is a satellite-based global notification system for methane super-emitters.
2. It is run by UNEP's International Methane Emissions Observatory.
3. It was launched at COP26 in Glasgow.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: MARS was launched at COP27 in Sharm el-Sheikh in 2022. It supports the Global Methane Pledge, which seeks a 30% cut from 2020 levels by 2030, and now covers coal mines and waste.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
With reference to carbon pricing, consider the following statements:
1. India's Carbon Credit Trading Scheme is an emission-intensity based trading system.
2. Industries that exceed their targets earn tradable Carbon Credit Certificates.
3. The World Bank's State and Trends of Carbon Pricing 2026 reports that carbon pricing covers 29% of global greenhouse gas emissions.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. Carbon taxes and ETS generated over 107 billion dollars in 2025.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
With reference to blended fuels in India, consider the following statements:
1. BIS published IS 19850:2026 for E22, E25, E27 and E30 fuels.
2. India has achieved the 20% ethanol blending target set under the National Policy on Biofuels, 2018.
3. China accounts for nearly 90% of the global DME production capacity.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. IS 18698:2026 covers DME-blended LPG and replaces the 2024 standard.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
With reference to geothermal energy in India, consider the following statements:
1. Ladakh's Puga Valley is to host India's first geothermal power plant with ONGC.
2. The Geological Survey of India has identified 381 hot springs in the country.
3. Geothermal energy is harnessed from heat stored in the Earth's crust.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. A 1 MWe pilot plant is planned and about 10,600 MW potential has been estimated; the National Policy on Geothermal Energy was issued in 2025.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
With reference to the Global Forest Goals Report 2026, consider the following statements:
1. Forest finance has already met the estimated annual need of 300 billion dollars.
2. It is prepared by UN DESA and the UN Forum on Forests secretariat.
3. Forest area shrank by over 40 million hectares between 2015 and 2025.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Forest finance reached a record 84 billion dollars in 2023, far below the estimated 300 billion dollars needed annually by 2030. The Strategic Plan for Forests covers 2017-2030.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q:
With reference to a heat dome, consider the following statements:
1. It is a high-pressure system that traps warm air near the surface.
2. It promotes cloud formation and cools the surface.
3. Descending air in it is compressed and heated.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: High pressure prevents cloud formation, which traps heat and causes heatwaves and droughts.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
With reference to parametric insurance, consider the following statements:
1. It pays a pre-agreed sum when a specified measurable event such as temperature or rainfall occurs.
2. It compensates for the actual physical damage assessed after the event.
3. It can offer faster relief during heatwaves and floods.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Parametric insurance pays on a trigger, not on assessed loss, which speeds up payouts.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
With reference to cheetahs and Project Cheetah, consider the following statements:
1. The cheetah is the only large carnivore declared extinct in India, in 1952.
2. Project Cheetah is implemented by the National Tiger Conservation Authority.
3. The Asiatic cheetah is classified as Vulnerable by IUCN.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The African cheetah is Vulnerable; the Asiatic cheetah is Critically Endangered. Cheetahs do not roar.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
With reference to the Indian soft-shell turtle, consider the following statements:
1. It is also known as the Ganges softshell turtle.
2. It is listed in Schedule I of the Wildlife Protection Act, 1972.
3. It is listed in CITES Appendix I and is Endangered on the IUCN Red List.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. The first satellite-tagged specimen was released in Kaziranga National Park.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
With reference to pangolins, consider the following statements:
1. The Chinese pangolin is found across most of the North-East of India and in peninsular India.
2. Pangolins are the only mammals completely covered with keratin scales.
3. Two pangolin species occur in India: the Indian and the Chinese pangolin.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The Chinese pangolin is found in Assam and the eastern Himalayas; the Indian pangolin occurs south of the Himalayas except most of the North-East.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
With reference to Prosopis juliflora, consider the following statements:
1. It is native to Mexico.
2. It is a native Indian species that supports biodiversity.
3. It is a phreatophyte that draws water from below the water table.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: It is an invasive species that reduces native plant diversity. It will be used as feedstock for India's first green methanol plant.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
Antarctic sea ice decline since 2015 is linked to which of the following?
1. Deep ocean heat
2. Stronger westerly winds
3. A self-reinforcing feedback loop
4. Weakening of the stratification that blocked heat
How many of the above are linked?
questions.why: All of them acted together: stronger westerlies drew warm salty deep water upward, melting sea ice, and the feedback made new ice formation harder.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the examination system in India, consider the following statements:
1. NTA conducts major higher education entrance examinations such as NEET-UG, JEE Main and CUET.
2. The K. Radhakrishnan Committee (2024) recommended restructuring the NTA to conduct only higher education entrance examinations.
3. Examination malpractice relates to the right to equality and equal opportunity under Articles 14 and 16.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. The committee also recommended a dedicated Director-General and ten specialised verticals.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the recommendations of the K. Radhakrishnan Committee (2024) on the National Testing Agency, consider the following statements:
1. It recommended at least 1,000 secure testing centres.
2. It recommended a hybrid process combining computer-based and paper-and-pencil testing.
3. It recommended that the NTA should also conduct all recruitment examinations.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: It recommended that the NTA conduct only higher education entrance examinations. It also proposed mobile testing centres and a DigiExam system with Aadhaar-based biometric authentication.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the NITI Aayog report on school education (2014-2024), consider the following statements:
1. Enrolment in government schools has risen to over 60% of total enrolment.
2. Primary-level dropout rate fell from 4.34% in 2014-15 to 0.3% in 2024-25.
3. Internet connectivity in schools rose to 63.5% in 2024-25.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Government schools' share of enrolment fell to 49.25%, while private unaided schools rose to 38.8%. GER declines to 78.7% at the secondary level and 58.4% at the higher secondary level.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to challenges in India's school education, consider the following statements:
1. Only about 5% of schools offer continuous Grade 1-12 education.
2. About 7% of schools operate with a single teacher.
3. About 50% of secondary public schools lack science labs.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. Secondary dropout remains high at 11.5%, and 1.19 lakh schools lack functional electricity.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the Sample Registration System Statistical Report 2024, consider the following statements:
1. India's Total Fertility Rate remained at 1.9, below the replacement level of 2.1.
2. The Sample Registration System is conducted by NITI Aayog.
3. Kerala recorded the lowest Infant Mortality Rate.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: SRS is conducted by the Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner, India, under the Ministry of Home Affairs.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the findings of the SRS Statistical Report 2024, consider the following statements:
1. Crude Birth Rate declined to 18.3.
2. Population aged 60 years and above reached 9.7%.
3. Sex ratio at birth improved to 918 females per 1,000 males.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. IMR was 24, U5MR was 28, and working-age population (15-59) was 66.4%.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to demographic indicators in India, consider the following statements:
1. Neonatal deaths account for about 73% of infant deaths.
2. Mean age of effective marriage for females rose to 23.1 years.
3. Institutional deliveries cover less than half of all births.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The report records 95.4% of deliveries receiving medical attention. Road accidents account for 3.2% of deaths and suicides 2.8%.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the Demographic Transition Theory, consider the following statements:
1. It describes a shift from high fertility and mortality to low fertility and mortality.
2. The term was first coined by Warren Thompson in 1929.
3. Replacement fertility rate is 2.1 children per woman.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. The theory was later developed by Frank Notestein in 1945; South Indian states have fertility of about 1.5.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the care economy as discussed in an EAC-PM working paper, consider the following statements:
1. India spends over 5% of its GDP on the care economy.
2. Unpaid domestic and care work by women is valued at about 15-17% of India's GDP.
3. Women spend about 289 minutes daily on unpaid domestic work against about 88 minutes by men.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: India spends less than 1% of GDP on the care economy. Time Use Survey 2024 provides the time-use data.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to government initiatives relating to the care economy, consider the following statements:
1. The Palna Scheme under Mission Shakti provides Anganwadi-cum-Crèches for children aged 6 months to 6 years.
2. Rashtriya Vayoshri Yojana provides assistive devices to low-income seniors.
3. Atal Vayo Abhyuday Yojana is an umbrella scheme for elderly welfare.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. The EAC-PM proposed a Parivar Seva Kosh and a Carepreneur Fund within a four-pillar framework.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to maternity and paternity provisions in India, consider the following statements:
1. The Maternity Benefit Act, 1961 provides 26 weeks of leave for women in establishments with more than 10 employees.
2. There is a dedicated statutory paternity leave law for the private sector.
3. Central government servants get 15 days of paternity leave under the Central Civil Services (Leave) Rules.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: No statutory paternity law exists for the private sector. Sikkim has extended paternity leave.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q: The primary-level dropout rate in 2024-25 as per the NITI Aayog report on school education is:
questions.why: It fell from 4.34% in 2014-15.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the NSO Survey on Household Social Consumption: Health, consider the following statements:
1. It was conducted during the NSS 80th round (January-December 2025).
2. Most diseases were identified through self-reporting, raising the chance of under or over reporting.
3. Over 60% of hospitalisation cases occur in public hospitals.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Over 60% of hospitalisations occur in private hospitals (57.9% rural, 64.6% urban). Average out-of-pocket expenditure is Rs 50,508 in private against Rs 6,631 in public hospitals.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to healthcare in India as highlighted in the survey, consider the following statements:
1. Government health expenditure is 1.43% of GDP against the National Health Policy 2017 target of 2.5%.
2. The doctor-population ratio of 1:811 includes both allopathic and AYUSH practitioners.
3. AMRIT pharmacies are managed by HLL Lifecare Limited.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. AMRIT pharmacies offer medicines at 50% to 90% discount. There is one rural PHC for about 33,800 people against the norm of 30,000.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to health schemes, consider the following statements:
1. Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY provides a cover of Rs 5 lakh per family per year for secondary and tertiary care.
2. Janani Suraksha Yojana is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme under the National Health Mission.
3. JANANI platform is a digital platform upgrading the RCH portal.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. JANANI stands for Journey of Antenatal, Natal and Neonatal Integrated Care and integrates with U-WIN and POSHAN.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the Right to Education framework in India, consider the following statements:
1. Article 45 directs the state to provide early childhood care for children below 3 years.
2. In Lucknow Public School v. State of Uttar Pradesh the Supreme Court held that neighbourhood schools must give immediate admission to eligible students.
3. Article 51A(k) places a duty on parents to provide educational opportunities to children aged 6 to 14.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Article 45 covers children below 6 years. The judgment reinforces the Common School System envisioned by the Kothari Commission.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the 'Women and Men in India 2025' report, consider the following statements:
1. Maternal Mortality Ratio fell from 254 in 2004-06 to 88 in 2021-23.
2. Women make up over 33% of the Members of Parliament.
3. Female voter turnout surpassed male turnout in the 2019 and 2024 general elections.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Women constitute 13.65% of MPs as of 2025 and hold 9.86% of ministerial portfolios. The report is published by MoSPI.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the 'Women and Men in India 2025' report, consider the following statements:
1. Sex ratio at birth improved from 904 in 2017-19 to 917 in 2021-23.
2. The gender gap in literacy rates is 14.4 percentage points.
3. Worker Population Ratio in 2025 is 76.6% for males and 38.8% for females.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. Female GER exceeds male GER at all school levels, and rural female LFPR rose from 37.5% to 45.9%.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the NCRB 'Crime in India 2024' report, consider the following statements:
1. Crime rate per lakh population dropped to 418.9 from 448.3.
2. Cyber crimes surged by 17.9%.
3. Crimes against Scheduled Tribes increased by over 20%.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Crimes against STs decreased by 23.1% and crimes against SCs by 3.6%. Crimes against senior citizens rose 16.9%.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the NCRB 'Accidental Deaths and Suicides in India 2024' report, consider the following statements:
1. Suicide rate in cities is lower than the all-India rate.
2. Rate of suicides per lakh population decreased from 12.3 to 12.2.
3. Over-speeding was the prime cause of road accidents.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The suicide rate in cities (16.3) is higher than the all-India rate (12.2). Family problems accounted for 33.5% of suicides, and Maharashtra reported the most.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the Supreme Court judgment in Shaheen Malik v. Union of India (2025), consider the following statements:
1. The Court invoked Article 142 to hold that forcible acid ingestion victims are covered as acid attack victims under the RPwD Act, 2016.
2. It held that acid sellers should not be made co-accused.
3. It suggested reversing the burden of proof onto the accused in acid attack cases.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The Court said acid sellers should be made co-accused. It also felt existing punishments had failed to deter such crimes.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the World Urban Forum, consider the following statements:
1. It is organised by UN-Habitat.
2. Its 13th session was held in Baku, Azerbaijan, with the theme 'Housing the World: Safe and Resilient Cities and Communities'.
3. The first session was held in Nairobi in 2002.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. The outcome document is the Baku Call to Action and the forum supports the New Urban Agenda (2016) and SDG 11.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q: The World Cities Report 2026 released by UN-Habitat is titled:
opts: Cities and Climate Action: Pathways to Resilience
The Global Housing Crisis: Pathways to Action
Informality and Urban Growth: Pathways to Action
Affordable Cities for All: Pathways to Equity
questions.why: Up to 3.4 billion people worldwide lack adequate housing.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
With reference to the private space sector in India, consider the following statements:
1. IN-SPACe was established in 2020 as a single-window agency to promote and authorise non-government entities.
2. NewSpace India Limited is the commercial arm of ISRO.
3. The Indian Space Association is a regulator under the Department of Space.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: ISpA is an industry body and policy think tank representing private space companies. It is not a regulator.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
With reference to FDI limits in the space sector under the Indian Space Policy framework, consider the following statements:
1. 100% FDI is allowed under the automatic route in satellite components and subsystems.
2. 74% FDI is allowed in satellite operations and ground segments.
3. 49% FDI is allowed in launch vehicles.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. Beyond these limits, government approval is required.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
With reference to financial support for space startups in India, consider the following statements:
1. The Rs 1,000 crore Venture Capital Fund is managed by SIDBI.
2. The Technology Adoption Fund is a Rs 500 crore fund to commercialise early-stage innovations.
3. IN-SPACe Seed Fund Scheme gives grants of up to Rs 1 crore.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. Spacetech startups rose from single digits in 2019 to over 400 by early 2026.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
With reference to the Indian space economy, consider the following statements:
1. India has already enacted a comprehensive Space Activities law.
2. It was valued at 8.4 billion dollars in 2023, about 2% of the global space economy.
3. The IN-SPACe Decadal Vision targets 44 billion dollars by 2033.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: India does not yet have a comprehensive space law; the Indian National Space Bill is yet to be finalised. Space Policy 2023 defines roles of stakeholders.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
With reference to UAV drone swarm systems, consider the following statements:
1. Drones in a swarm coordinate directly with each other rather than only relying on a central controller.
2. The Atlas drone swarm system was unveiled by India.
3. A swarm can continue its mission even if some drones are destroyed.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Atlas is a Chinese AI-enabled swarm system by China Electronics Technology Group Corporation. India's examples include Chanakya and Project Samadh.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
With reference to NITI Aayog's report on Ease of Doing Research and Development, consider the following statements:
1. India's GERD is about 0.65% of GDP.
2. The report recommends raising R&D investment to at least 2% of GDP in 4-5 years.
3. The report recommends creating a 'Vigyan Nidhi' as a digital fellowship platform.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. Researcher density is 262 per million FTE against 4,821 in the USA; IITs receive over 80% of ANRF funding.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
With reference to research and innovation initiatives in India, consider the following statements:
1. The Anusandhan National Research Foundation functions under the Department of Science and Technology.
2. National Quantum Mission established four Thematic Hubs including at IISc Bengaluru for Quantum Computing.
3. Atal Innovation Mission was launched in 2016.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. NM-ICPS has established 25 Technology Innovation Hubs.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
With reference to orbital data centres, consider the following statements:
1. India's first AI orbital data centre satellite Pathfinder is to be built by Pixxel and Sarvam.
2. In a dawn-dusk sun-synchronous orbit they can use continuous solar power.
3. They need large quantities of freshwater for cooling.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Space acts as a cold heat sink so freshwater is not needed for cooling. A 40 MW terrestrial cluster can use over 1 million tonnes of water annually.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
With reference to Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X) communication, consider the following statements:
1. V2X excludes communication between vehicles and pedestrians.
2. TRAI's consultation paper identifies Cellular-V2X as the preferred technology.
3. DSRC uses Wi-Fi-based technology.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
