questions.why: V2X includes vehicle-to-vehicle, infrastructure, pedestrian and network communication.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
With reference to a scramjet propulsion system, consider the following statements:
1. It allows combustion of fuel to occur supersonically.
2. It uses atmospheric oxygen as the oxidiser.
3. DRDO's actively cooled full scale scramjet combustor achieved a run time of over 1,200 seconds.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. The earlier run time was 700 seconds. Fuels include hydrogen and endothermic liquid hydrocarbons.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
With reference to Mission Drishti, consider the following statements:
1. It is the world's first OptoSAR satellite developed by GalaxEye.
2. It was launched on an ISRO PSLV.
3. OptoSAR combines multispectral imaging and Synthetic Aperture Radar on a single platform.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: It was launched aboard SpaceX's Falcon 9. SAR can see through clouds and at night, while optical sensors give intuitive images.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
With reference to India's Venus Orbiter Mission, consider the following statements:
1. It was approved in 2024.
2. LVM-3 has been identified as the candidate launch vehicle.
3. Sweden has joined the mission.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. Launch is planned for March 2028 into an elliptical parking orbit.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
With reference to the SMILE mission, consider the following statements:
1. It is a joint mission of the European Space Agency and the Chinese Academy of Sciences.
2. It aims to capture panoramic imaging of the interaction between the solar wind and Earth's magnetosphere.
3. It carries the world's first space-borne soft X-ray imager.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. It was launched aboard a Vega-C rocket from French Guiana.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
With reference to the Sun and the Vela Supercluster, consider the following statements:
1. The Sun's corona is about a million degrees Celsius, much hotter than the photosphere at about 5,500 degrees Celsius.
2. Alfvenic or kink waves are transverse magnetohydrodynamic waves in the corona.
3. The Vela Supercluster lies in the Zone of Avoidance, an area obscured by the Milky Way's dust and stars.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. Vela spans about 300 million light-years and is more massive than Laniakea, the supercluster containing the Milky Way.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
With reference to the Zwan-Wolf effect and the MAVEN mission, consider the following statements:
1. MAVEN is a NASA orbiter surveying the upper Martian atmosphere.
2. The Zwan-Wolf effect squeezes charged particles along flux tubes.
3. Its first observation in a planetary atmosphere was made by India's Mangalyaan.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The observation was made using data from NASA's MAVEN mission.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
With reference to Chandrayaan-3, consider the following statements:
1. It was honoured with the 2026 Goddard Astronautics Award of the American Institute of Aeronautics and Astronautics.
2. It made a soft landing near the Moon's South Pole on 23 August 2023.
3. It had a planned mission life of one lunar day.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. The mission had the Vikram lander and the Pragyan rover.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
With reference to the Cell Broadcast System launched in India, consider the following statements:
1. It broadcasts geo-targeted alerts simultaneously to mobile devices in a defined area.
2. It was developed by C-DOT under the Department of Telecommunications.
3. It is integrated with the CAP-based SACHET platform.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. It overcomes the limits of SMS-based alerts.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
With reference to egocentric data, consider the following statements:
1. It consists of recordings captured from the perspective of the person doing a task.
2. It is useful to train Vision-Language-Action models.
3. It raises concerns about surveillance, consent and compensation.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. It is collected by head, chest or wrist-mounted cameras.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
With reference to the 79th World Health Assembly, consider the following statements:
1. It adopted the second Global Action Plan on Antimicrobial Resistance for 2026-2036.
2. The Quadripartite partners are WHO, FAO, UNEP and WOAH.
3. It adopted the first resolution on radiation and health.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. The target is a 10% reduction in bacterial AMR-associated deaths by 2030; AMR may cause up to 39 million deaths by 2050.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
With reference to hepatitis, consider the following statements:
1. Hepatitis A, B and C are all spread only through contaminated water.
2. Hepatitis types B and C lead to chronic disease.
3. Hepatitis A and E are typically caused by contaminated food or water.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Hepatitis B, C and D typically spread through parenteral contact with infected body fluids.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
With reference to recent health developments, consider the following statements:
1. Polycystic ovary syndrome has been renamed Polyendocrine Metabolic Ovarian Syndrome.
2. Hantaviruses are zoonotic viruses carried by rodents.
3. Primary Amebic Meningoencephalitis caused by Naegleria fowleri is always fatal.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct per the magazine. Naegleria fowleri enters through the nose and lives in warm fresh water; hantavirus has no specific cure.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
With reference to the Ayush Grid Initiative, consider the following statements:
1. It was launched by the Ministry of Ayush in 2018.
2. Ayush Hospital Management Information System and e-Aushadhi are developed under it.
3. The Ayush Anudan Portal digitises grant proposals.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct.

questions.subject: Art & Culture
questions.q:
With reference to the Bhojshala complex at Dhar, consider the following statements:
1. It was built by the Paramara king Bhoja in the 11th century.
2. The Madhya Pradesh High Court declared it a protected monument under the AMASR Act, 1958.
3. The court based its ruling on Articles 25 and 26 of the Constitution.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. The ruling quashed the 2003 ASI order and directed efforts to bring back the Saraswati idol held in the British Museum.

questions.subject: History
questions.q:
With reference to the Paramara king Bhoja, consider the following statements:
1. He was a contemporary of the Chola king Rajendra I.
2. He founded the city of Bhojpur on the banks of the Ganga.
3. He is credited with the architectural treatise Samarangana Sutradhara.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Bhojpur lies on the banks of the Betwa. He built the Bhojeshwar temple and the Upper Lake in Bhopal on the Kolans river.

questions.subject: Art & Culture
questions.q:
With reference to the Bhumija style of temple architecture, consider the following statements:
1. It is an evolved form of the Nagara style with some Dravida influences.
2. The shikhara has miniature replica spires arranged in tiers.
3. Most Paramara temples are of the Panchayatana type.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. The term means 'earth-born'.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the Padma Awards, consider the following statements:
1. They were instituted in 1954.
2. They are not titles under Article 18 and cannot be used with names.
3. Government servants are not eligible, except doctors and scientists.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. The Padma Awards Committee is headed by the Cabinet Secretary and constituted annually by the Prime Minister.

questions.subject: Art & Culture
questions.q:
With reference to the Somnath Temple, consider the following statements:
1. It is one of the twelve Jyotirlingas located at Prabhas Patan in Gujarat.
2. Ahilyabai Holkar restored it in the 18th century.
3. Its Pran Pratishtha in 1951 was performed by Dr. Rajendra Prasad.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. The temple was attacked by Mahmud Ghazni in 1026 and is mentioned by Al-Biruni.

questions.subject: History
questions.q:
With reference to the Leiden copper plates returned by the Netherlands, consider the following statements:
1. They bear the seal of the Chola king Rajendra Chola I.
2. They record the grant of the village of Anaimangalam to a Buddhist vihara built by Srivijaya rulers.
3. They were taken to the Netherlands in the 17th century from Madurai.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: They were taken in 1712 from Nagapattinam by Florentius Camper. The earliest known copper plate inscription is the Sogaura plate of the Mauryan era.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to the Korean War and India's role, consider the following statements:
1. A 1953 armistice ended the conflict with a formal peace treaty.
2. Korea was divided along the 38th Parallel after World War II.
3. India's contribution included the 60 Para Field Ambulance and the Custodian Force of India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The 1953 armistice divided the peninsula near the 38th parallel but no peace treaty was signed. A memorial was inaugurated at Imjingak Park in Seoul.

questions.subject: Art & Culture
questions.q:
With reference to the International Booker Prize, consider the following statements:
1. It is awarded for a single book translated into English and published in the UK or Ireland.
2. Banu Mushtaq's Heart Lamp was translated from Malayalam.
3. Geetanjali Shree's Tomb of Sand was the first Hindi work to win.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Heart Lamp is the first Kannada work to win, translated by Deepa Bhasthi in 2025.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the ethics and economics of wages in India, consider the following statements:
1. Article 43 of the Directive Principles speaks of a living wage for workers.
2. Article 39(d) relates to equal pay for equal work for men and women.
3. Article 43 is a Fundamental Right enforceable against employers.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Articles 39(d), 41 and 43 are Directive Principles, which are non-justiciable. The magazine also notes a government search for a unified National Floor Wage Rate.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to wage justice challenges in India, consider the following statements:
1. India has fewer than 10,000 labour inspectors for a workforce of over 50 crore.
2. About 90% of India's workforce is informal.
3. The 'state competition trap' refers to States informally signalling flexible labour enforcement to attract FDI.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. The 'race to the bottom' lowers worker protections.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the Samagra Shiksha Scheme, consider the following statements:
1. The funding ratio for North-Eastern and Himalayan States is 75:25.
2. It was launched in 2018 and subsumed Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan, Rashtriya Madhyamik Shiksha Abhiyan and the Teacher Education Scheme.
3. It is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme with 60:40 Centre-State funding for most States.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The ratio for North-Eastern and Himalayan States is 90:10. Union Territories without a legislature get 100% central assistance.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the Samagra Shiksha Scheme, consider the following statements:
1. The Governing Council is headed by the Minister of Education.
2. Nipun Bharat, the mission for foundational literacy and numeracy, is launched under the scheme.
3. It supports PARAKH, the National Assessment Centre.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. The scheme was extended till 30 September 2026 or until approval for the 16th Finance Commission cycle.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to PM POSHAN, consider the following statements:
1. It was earlier known as the Mid-Day Meal Scheme, and began as the National Programme of Nutritional Support to Primary Education in 1995.
2. It extends hot cooked meals to Balvatika (pre-Class I) children.
3. Tithi Bhojan involves community participation by providing special meals on festivals.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. Social audits are mandatory in all districts, and PM POSHAN covers about 11.8 crore children.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to nutrition norms under PM POSHAN, consider the following statements:
1. Primary stage meals provide 450 kcal and 12 g protein.
2. The scheme is a Central Sector Scheme with 100% central funding.
3. Upper primary meals provide 700 kcal and 20 g protein.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: It is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme with 60:40 Centre-State sharing, under the Ministry of Education. Primary food grain norm is 100 g and upper primary 150 g.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the Rashtriya Bal Swasthya Karyakram (RBSK) 2.0 guidelines, consider the following statements:
1. RBSK was launched in 2013 and covers children from birth to 18 years.
2. RBSK 2.0 covers 38 common health conditions.
3. The 4Ds are Defects at birth, Diseases, Deficiencies and Developmental delays.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. District Early Intervention Centres provide comprehensive management and RBSK 2.0 adds mental health conditions and NCD risk factors.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to screening platforms under RBSK, consider the following statements:
1. Newborns from birth to 6 weeks are screened at delivery points.
2. Children from 6 weeks to 6 years are screened at Anganwadi Centres.
3. Students from 6 to 18 years are screened in government and government-aided schools.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. Tertiary care including cochlear implants is provided under the programme through the National Health Mission.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q: The Samagra Shiksha Scheme is implemented by which ministry?
opts: Ministry of Women and Child Development
Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship
questions.why: It is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme under the Ministry of Education.
